description: Daily congressional floor vote with structured For/Against speaker debate, vote tally bar, and sentiment pulse.

billId.source: Congress.gov or roll call record header

billIdSlug.description: URL-safe bill ID for snapId and channel strings

billShortTitle.rule: Use the popular name if one exists (e.g. 'PROTECT Kids Act'); fall back to a compressed version of the official title

billFullTitle.description: Full official bill title as it appears in Congress.gov

voteOutcome.description: Short outcome string, include vote count

policyAreaSlug.description: CamelCase slug of policyArea for channel string
policyAreaSlug.rule: Remove spaces and punctuation, capitalize each word: 'Armed Forces and National Security' → 'ArmedForcesAndNationalSecurity'

primaryRepId.description: Bioguide ID of the primary FOR speaker (use sponsor or leading proponent)

voteFor.source: senate.gov roll call XML OR clerk.house.gov roll call XML

voteAbstain.description: Number of Not Voting / Present / Abstain votes

speaker1Name.description: Full name of first FOR speaker (typically bill sponsor or committee chair)

speaker1Title.description: Party abbreviation, state, and role (e.g. 'R-MI · House E&C Committee')

speaker1Quote.description: Direct floor quote, max 220 characters. Must be an actual quote or closely paraphrased from the Congressional Record.

speaker2Name.description: Full name of second FOR speaker — ideally cross-party to show bipartisanship
speaker2Name.rule: Prefer a speaker from the opposite party to speaker1 when bipartisan support exists

speaker3Name.description: Full name of the AGAINST speaker (opposition voice)
speaker3Name.rule: Must be from the opposing side. If vote was bipartisan, use a notable dissenter.

summaryText.description: Neutral 2-4 sentence summary: what the bill does, vote margin, notable crossovers, next step.
summaryText.rule: Neutral framing. Include vote count. Note any bipartisan crossover. State next legislative step (sent to Senate / signed / vetoed).

sentimentQuestion.description: Policy-framed public opinion question (NOT 'did you like this vote'). Must be answerable by any constituent regardless of party.
sentimentQuestion.rule: Frame as a policy outcome question. 4 options required. Options must span the realistic opinion space.

sourceLabel.description: Human-readable source label for Trust.Thread sources[].name

sourceUrl.description: Direct URL to the official roll call record — goes into Trust.Thread sources[].url ONLY (not in any other element)

verificationLevel.rule: Use 'Tier 3' for primary government sources (congress.gov, senate.gov, clerk.house.gov). Use 'VERIFIED' when combining multiple primary-government sources.

spawnRef.description: SPAWN file ID this snap traces back to

auditDate.description: ISO date this snap was audited/generated (YYYY-MM-DD)

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 datetime this snap was created

speakerSelectionRules: speaker1: Primary sponsor or committee chair who led floor management of the bill (position: For)
speaker2: Ideally a cross-party co-sponsor or notable bipartisan supporter (position: For). If no crossover exists, use a second prominent supporter from same party.
speaker3: The most prominent or articulate dissenter who spoke against (position: Against)

fallbackRules.onRecess: Use most recent active session within 14 calendar days. Display advisory: 'No floor activity on {date} — showing most recent session ({fallbackDate})'.
fallbackRules.onNoVote: Skip bill, replace with next ranked bill from the same session. Minimum 3 snaps per run.
fallbackRules.onApiFailure: Fall back to direct scraping of senate.gov or clerk.house.gov XML roll call files.
fallbackRules.onNoBioguideMatch: Log warning in NORM file. Use first speaker's bioguide as primaryRepId. Do not block snap generation.
